publisher: Various London printers and publishers (five American sheets from Boston and Cambridge, Massachusetts)

digital.name: EEBO-TCP
digital.id: 674 TCP texts (A-, B- and N-series numbers, e.g. A56102, B03301; the number is in each poem's note)

note: A collection of 674 broadside ballads, each one a separate single-sheet print transcribed by the Text Creation Partnership: 382 A-series, 287 B-series and 5 N-series numbers (the N-series ones, from Evans-TCP, are early American sheets printed in Massachusetts, at Boston and Cambridge). Every one of the 674 TCP numbers named in the poem notes was found in the TCP master list (github.com/textcreationpartnership/Texts, TCP.csv), whose dates run from 1540 to 1700; the imprints differ from sheet to sheet, so no single publisher is given. Spot checks: 8 poems chosen at random were compared with their TCP XML files and 37 of 40 sampled lines were found (the rest differ in spelling or punctuation). Examples of the sheet imprints in the TCP headers: A56102 'The Protestants sweet orange, or, Sower sawce for popery. Printed for J. Back, [London, 1689?]'; B03301 'Enfield Common. Printed for Charles Bates at the Sun and Bible in Pye-corner, [London, 1695?]'. The group takes in 645 poems of 'Anonymous (English broadside ballads)', 15 of Martin Parker, 8 of Laurence Price and 6 of Thomas D'Urfey; the printed sheets are the sources, and the page-image sources are Early English Books Online (ProQuest). To cite a single ballad, use the TCP number in that poem's note; this record cites the collection only.
